title: edikt hook registration surface (SP-007)
description: The DATA-driven registration surface SP-007 requires: edikt hook run <name> resolves names from this file, never from a hardcoded Go enumeration. Ships at templates/hooks/registry.yaml (tier-1, INV-001 permits .yaml). Read at runtime by three independent consumers who must never drift apart: (1) the shim generator, which renders one templates/hooks/<file> per row from the canonical FR-004 template; (2) tools/edikt/internal/hook's registry.go, which asserts every row with status:migrated has a matching Go-side Register() call (registry_test.go, the SP-007 parity gate); (3) the corpus recorder (SR-009), which iterates this file to know which hooks to run the bash oracle against and where each hook's matrix lives. A name absent from this file is unregistered — edikt hook run <name> for an unregistered name never silently no-ops (SP-007); it exits 0 (fail-open per the hook tier's standing posture) but journals a distinctly-typed 'unregistered-hook-name' cause and writes a loud stderr diagnostic.

name.description: The <name> argument to `edikt hook run <name>` and the token substituted into the canonical shim template. Matches the .sh basename minus extension for every directly-registered hook.

event.description: The Claude Code lifecycle event key this hook is registered under in templates/settings.json.tmpl's hooks: block, drawn from the closed set of event keys this template actually declares (e.g. "PreToolUse"), or the literal "statusLine" for the one hook registered under that top-level key instead of the hooks: block (status-line.sh — the sole payload-invoked hook outside hooks:), or null for a sourced bash library (class: library) that is never itself registered or invoked with a hook payload on stdin. Required and enum-closed per the SPEC-014 pre-flight correction: before this field was required with a closed enum, a typo such as "PreToolUSe" validated cleanly against the open string type, silently producing a registry row that would never actually fire.

file.description: Filename under templates/hooks/ this row governs.

class.description: gate = the three write-deny hooks (pre-tool-use, verify-gate, inject-directives-pre), migrated last per FR-007. multi-call = stop-hook, phase-end-detector, subagent-stop, migrated second. injector = every other directly-registered hook, migrated first (parallel with the installer track). library = a sourced bash helper (the deleted event-log.sh helper (see ADR-058's 2026-08-23 amendment), _plan-naming.sh) with no direct Claude Code registration — see spec.md 'Existing Architecture' for how its python3 removal is handled without a shim of its own.

status.description: pending = still the pre-FR-004 hand-written bash+python3 body. migrated = swapped to the FR-004 exec shim, with a corresponding Go handler registered under tools/edikt/internal/hook. Flips exactly once, per-hook, per FR-007's per-hook-not-per-batch rule.

shape.description: WHAT the shipped templates/hooks/<file> is, read by the byte-stability gate (tools/edikt/check/hook-shim-byte-stability.sh, via `edikt hook shim check`). Absent or "exec-shim" — the default for 21 of 22 rows — means the canonical FR-004 exec shim, whose shipped bytes are diffed against a fresh render of the canonical template and must match it exactly. "dispatch-orchestrator" is the ADR-063 Amendment (2026-08-22) second shape, admitted for a hook that must perform genuine multi-round-trip LLM dispatch itself because INV-012 forbids the tier-2 binary from exec'ing a model: its body is deliberately NOT the canonical render, so the gate asserts its declared properties (non-empty, zero python3 invocation sites, execs `hook run <name>`) instead of diffing it, and reports it as its own subject count rather than skipping it silently. Declared as DATA rather than hardcoded in the gate for the same SP-007 reason `name` is — a second such hook must be a registry edit, not a binary edit.
shape.$comment: A row omitting this field is an exec shim. Adding a THIRD value requires amending ADR-063, whose Amendment scopes the second shape to phase-end-detector and requires any future claimant to demonstrate genuine multi-round-trip dispatch.

python3_baseline_count.description: Informational only — the python3 invocation count measured at spec-authoring time (re-measured from ADR-058's stale 19-of-22 figure), carried here so a reader can see the per-hook removal target without re-running grep. Not consumed by any gate; drifts out of date the moment a hook migrates and that is expected.

retired.description: Hooks that once had a row under `hooks` and no longer run (the write-time channel's retirement took verify-gate and inject-directives-pre with it; see the changelog). A name here is NOT registered — `edikt hook run <name>` journals unregistered-hook-name for it exactly as for a name that never existed. The list exists so `edikt upgrade`'s settings reconciliation and `edikt doctor` can name a settings.json entry that still registers one of these as 'retired — run /edikt:upgrade' rather than 'unknown hook'. A retired hook's history (its corpus matrix, its python3 baseline) is the record of the channel it served; it is not carried here.

event.description: The Claude Code event the hook was registered under, so a settings.json entry can be matched by event and command basename.

since.description: The first edikt version that ships without the hook. The decision that retired it is named in that version's changelog entry.
